in a simplified bacterial community composed of three species with different morphological responses to grazing and starvation, the relative success of a species depended on the availability of nutrients and on the presence of predators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative success of different bacterial species is not only determined by the ability to escape predation but also by their ability to adapt to the prevailing environmental conditions.
the relative success of different bacterial strains in a community depends on their response to predation and the level of nutrients available in the environment.
